archetypes.name: sync-invariant
archetypes.rationale: The plan creates a 4-way canonical-clause sync contract but the drift-guard test only greps voting-protocol.md — the two SKILL.md copies are protected only by documentation and indirect lint, leaving a CI gap the plan does not explicitly justify.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine every consumer listed in the plan's 4-way canonical-clause sync contract (render-voter-prompt.sh output, skills/shared/voting-protocol.md, skills/design/SKILL.md Step 3 MAV, skills/implement/SKILL.md Step 5 MAV) and verify whether the drift-guard test case hard-codes a grep assertion against each consumer or leaves some copies unguarded. Identify which copies the plan explicitly guarantees via CI versus which are protected only by documentation or indirect linting paths like lint-references-headers. Check whether the render-voter-prompt.md edit-in-sync rules are sufficient as a process-only guard, or whether CI needs explicit grep assertions for the SKILL.md copies to prevent silent drift. Verify that any future edit to the canonical clause text in just one SKILL.md copy would be caught by at least one failing CI target before merge, and flag if the plan relies solely on human discipline for two of the four copies. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: grammar-clause-scope
archetypes.rationale: The canonical OOS clause text contains a grammar-specific parenthetical ('or OOS_N: items in plan review') that is irrelevant when emitted under finding-only grammar for /review voters, and the plan does not address whether this text should be parameterized or conditionally suppressed per grammar variant.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the canonical OOS clause text as specified in the plan's render-voter-prompt.sh output contract and compare it against what /review voters actually receive in their ballot — FINDING_N items that may carry an [OUT_OF_SCOPE] prefix, never OOS_N items. Determine whether the parenthetical 'or OOS_N: items in plan review' in the unified clause creates ambiguity or misleads /review voters when emitted under --id-grammar finding-only, given those voters have no OOS_N ballot entries to vote on. Check whether the plan addresses this discrepancy anywhere via a helper flag, conditional clause emission, or grammar-parameterized clause text in the proposed implementation. Verify that the test case for finding-only grammar asserts the OOS clause is present but does not assert that grammar-irrelevant parentheticals are absent or suppressed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
